correctness.rationale: Let a=v^T A^{-1}v, m=v^TAv, tau=||A^{-1}v-av||>0, u=(A^{-1}v-av)/tau, r=||(I-P2)Av||>0, w=(I-P2)Av/r, and P3 project onto span{v,u,w}. From Au=(v-aAv)/tau, the third mixed candidate is nonzero when a!=0. Multiplying A v=m v+((1-am)/tau)u+r w by A^{-1} and projecting orthogonally to P3 yields (I-P3)A^{-1}w=-[(1-am)/(tau*r)](I-P3)A^{-1}u. Thus premature fourth mixed breakdown with continuing split channel occurs exactly when am=1 and the four Laurent vectors A^{-2}v,A^{-1}v,v,Av are independent. Independence requires at least four distinct eigenvalues active in v: a polynomial of degree <=3 cannot have more than three distinct spectral roots; conversely four active points give independent Laurent vectors by multiplication by A^2. For either definite sign Cauchy-Schwarz forces am>=1, with equality only for a one-eigenvalue vector; indefinite four-distinct spectra permit positive spectral weights with am<1 and >1, and continuity gives am=1 while all four weights stay nonzero. Independent exact SymPy projector calculations for diag(-1,1,2,3) and v=(sqrt3,sqrt56,3,3)/sqrt77 yield a=11/14, m=14/11, tau²=103/539, r²=564/847, fourth split squared=14112/498623>0, mixed squared=0. These exact numbers corroborate the fully quantified spectral proof.

final_claim: In exact arithmetic for real nonsingular symmetric A and unit starting v, inverse-leading mixed extended-Krylov construction can build three vectors and then have a zero fourth mixed candidate although the fourth split candidate is nonzero if and only if A has both positive and negative eigenvalues and at least four distinct eigenvalues. The fourth projected mixed residual equals a scalar (proportional to 1-(v^T A^{-1}v)(v^TAv)) times the fourth split residual. The sharp 4x4 example diag(-1,1,2,3) has condition number three and exact residual squares.
